lines: In spite of "endless talk of difference," American society is an amazing machine for **homogenizing** people. There is "the democratizing uniformity of dress and discourse, and the casualness and absence of deference" characteristic of popular culture. People are absorbed into "a culture of consumption" launched by the 19th-century department stores that offered "vast arrays of goods in an elegant atmosphere. Instead of intimate shops catering to a knowledgeable elite" these were stores "anyone could enter, regardless of class or background. This turned shopping into a public and democratic act." The mass media, advertising and sports are other forces for homogenization.

尽管人们“不断谈论差异”，美国社会仍是一部惊人的、使人趋于同质的机器。这里存在大众文化特有的“着装和言谈的平等化与统一性，以及随意和不讲尊卑的作风”。人们被纳入19世纪百货商店开创的“消费文化”之中，这些商店“在优雅的环境里提供琳琅满目的商品。这些商店不是迎合见多识广的精英的私密小店”，而是“不论阶层或背景，任何人都能进入的商店。这使购物成为一种公共的、平等的活动”。大众媒体、广告和体育运动也是促进同质化的力量。

lines: Immigrants are quickly fitting into this common culture, which may not be altogether elevating but is hardly poisonous. Writing for the National Immigration Forum, Gregory Rodriguez reports that today's immigration is neither at unprecedented levels nor resistant to assimilation. In 1998 immigrants were 9.8 percent of the population; in 1900, 13.6 percent. In the 10 years prior to 1990, 3.1 immigrants arrived for every 1,000 residents; in the 10 years prior to 1890, 9.2 for every 1,000. Now, consider three indices of assimilation — language, home ownership and intermarriage.

移民正在迅速融入这一共同文化，这种文化也许算不上多么高雅，但也绝无毒性。格雷戈里·罗德里格斯为全国移民论坛撰文指出，如今的移民既没有达到空前的规模，也不抗拒同化。1998年，移民占人口的9.8%；而在1900年是13.6%。在1990年之前的十年间，每1000名居民中有3.1名移民迁入；而1890年之前的十年间，每1000名居民中迁入9.2名。现在，让我们看看同化的三个指标——语言、住房所有权和异族通婚。

lines: The 1990 Census revealed that "a majority of immigrants from each of the fifteen most common countries of origin spoke English 'well' or 'very well' after ten years of residence." The children of immigrants tend to be bilingual and proficient in English. "By the third generation, the original language is lost in the majority of immigrant families." Hence the description of America as a "graveyard" for languages. By 1996, foreign-born immigrants who had arrived before 1970 had a home ownership rate of 75.6 percent, higher than the 69.8 percent rate among native-born Americans. Foreign-born Asians and Hispanics "have higher rates of intermarriage than do U.S.-born whites and blacks." By the third generation, one third of Hispanic women are married to non-Hispanics, and 41 percent of Asian-American women are married to non-Asians.

lines: Stratford-on-Avon, as we all know, has only one industry — William Shakespeare — but there are two distinctly separate and increasingly hostile branches. There is the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which presents superb productions of the plays at the Shakespeare Memorial Theatre on the Avon. And there are the townsfolk who largely live off the tourists who come, not to see the plays, but to look at Anne Hathaway's Cottage, Shakespeare's birthplace and the other sights.
众所周知，埃文河畔斯特拉特福镇只有一个产业——威廉·莎士比亚——但它分裂成两个截然不同、且日益敌对的分支。一个是皇家莎士比亚公司（RSC），在埃文河畔的莎士比亚纪念剧院上演精彩纷呈的莎剧。另一个是镇上居民，他们主要靠游客谋生——这些游客不是来看戏的，而是来看安妮·海瑟薇小屋、莎士比亚出生地和其他景点的。

lines: The tourist streams are not entirely separate. The sightseers who come by bus — and often take in Warwick Castle and Blenheim Palace on the side — don't usually see the plays, and some of them are even surprised to find a theatre in Stratford. However, the playgoers do manage a little sight-seeing along with their playgoing. It is the playgoers, the RSC contends, who bring in much of the town's revenue because they spend the night (some of them four or five nights) pouring cash into the hotels and restaurants. The sightseers can take in everything and get out of town by nightfall.
游客流并非完全分道而行。乘大巴前来的观光客——顺道往往还去沃里克城堡和布伦海姆宫——通常不看戏，有些人甚至惊讶地发现斯特拉特福居然有一座剧院。然而，看戏的人确实也会顺带游览观光。皇家莎士比亚公司声称，正是这些戏迷给小镇带来了大部分收入，因为他们要在此过夜（有些人住上四五晚），把大把钞票花进旅馆和餐馆。而观光客看完全部景点，天黑前就能离镇而去。

lines: That the seas are being overfished has been known for years. What researchers such as Ransom Myers and Boris Worm have shown is just how fast things are changing. They have looked at half a century of data from fisheries around the world. Their methods do not attempt to estimate the actual **biomass** (the amount of living biological matter) of fish species in particular parts of the ocean, but rather changes in that biomass over time. According to their latest paper published in Nature, the biomass of large predators (animals that kill and eat other animals) in a new fishery is reduced on average by 80% within 15 years of the start of exploitation. In some long-fished areas, it has halved again since then.

海洋正遭到过度捕捞，这一点人们多年来早有所知。而兰塞姆·迈尔斯和鲍里斯·沃尔姆等研究者所揭示的，是事情变化的速度之快。他们分析了世界各地渔场半个世纪以来的数据。他们的方法并不试图估算海洋特定区域内鱼类物种的实际生物量（活体生物的总量），而是估算这一生物量随时间发生的变化。根据他们发表在《自然》杂志上的最新论文，在开始开发的15年内，新渔场中大型捕食动物的生物量平均减少80%。而在一些长期捕捞的海域，此后又减半。

lines: Dr. Worm acknowledges that these figures are conservative. One reason for this is that fishing technology has improved. Today's vessels can find their prey using satellites and sonar, which were not available 50 years ago. That means a higher proportion of what is in the sea is being caught, so the real difference between present and past is likely to be worse than the one recorded by changes in catch sizes. In the early days, too, longlines would have been more saturated with fish. Some individuals would therefore not have been caught, since no baited hooks would have been available to trap them, leading to an underestimate of fish stocks in the past. Furthermore, in the early days of longline fishing, a lot of fish were lost to sharks after they had been hooked. That is no longer a problem, because there are fewer sharks around now.

lines: Dr. Myers and Dr. Worm argue that their work gives a correct baseline, which future management efforts must take into account. They believe the data support an idea current among marine biologists, that of the "shifting baseline". The notion is that people have failed to detect the massive changes which have happened in the ocean because they have been looking back only a relatively short time into the past. That matters because theory suggests that the maximum sustainable yield that can be cropped from a fishery comes when the biomass of a target species is about 50% of its original levels. Most fisheries are well below that, which is a bad way to do business.

迈尔斯博士和沃尔姆博士认为，他们的研究给出了一个正确的基线，未来的渔业管理必须将其考虑在内。他们相信，这些数据支持了海洋生物学界流行的一种观点——“变动的基线”。这一观念是说，人们之所以未能察觉海洋中已经发生的巨大变化，是因为他们回望过去的时间跨度太短。这一点至关重要，因为理论表明，当目标物种的生物量约为其原始水平的50%时，渔场才能获得最大可持续产量。而大多数渔场都远低于这一水平，这可不是经营生意的正道。

lines: But what we forget — what our economy depends on us forgetting — is that happiness is more than pleasure without pain. The things that bring the greatest joy carry the greatest potential for loss and disappointment. Today, surrounded by promises of easy happiness, we need art to tell us, as religion once did, Memento mori: remember that you will die, that everything ends, and that happiness comes not in denying this but in living with it. It's a message even more bitter than a clove cigarette, yet, somehow, a breath of fresh air.
但我们忘记了——我们的经济恰恰依赖我们忘记这一点——幸福远不止是没有痛苦的快乐。带来最大欢乐的事物，也潜藏着最大的失落与失望。今天，在唾手可得的幸福承诺的包围中，我们需要艺术像宗教当年那样告诫我们：记住你终有一死，万物终有尽头，幸福不在于否认这一点，而在于与之共存。这一讯息比丁香烟还要苦涩，然而不知为何，却宛若一缕清新的空气。

lines: First, the object of our study pleads for definition. What is an intellectual? (46) I shall define him as an individual who has elected as his primary duty and pleasure in life the activity of thinking in a Socratic (苏格拉底) way about moral problems. He explores such problems consciously, articulately, and frankly, first by asking factual questions, then by asking moral questions, finally by suggesting action which seems appropriate in the light of the factual and moral information which he has obtained. (47) His function is analogous to that of a judge, who must accept the obligation of revealing in as obvious a manner as possible the course of reasoning which led him to his decision.
首先，我们的研究对象亟须界定。什么是知识分子？(46) 我将把他定义为这样一种人：他把以苏格拉底的方式思考道德问题作为人生的首要职责和乐趣。他自觉地、清晰地、坦率地探究这些问题：首先提出事实问题，继而提出道德问题，最后根据所获得的事实和道德方面的信息，提出看起来恰当的行动建议。(47) 知识分子的作用与法官相似，法官必须承担这样的义务：尽可能清楚地公开自己作出判决的推理过程。

lines: This definition excludes many individuals usually referred to as intellectuals — the average scientist, for one. (48) I have excluded him because, while his accomplishments may contribute to the solution of moral problems, he has not been charged with the task of approaching any but the factual aspects of those problems. Like other human beings, he encounters moral issues even in the everyday performance of his routine duties — he is not supposed to cook his experiments, manufacture evidence, or doctor his reports. (49) But his primary task is not to think about the moral code which governs his activity, any more than a businessman is expected to dedicate his energies to an exploration of rules of conduct in business. During most of his waking life he will take his code for granted, as the businessman takes his ethics.

这一定义把许多通常被称为知识分子的人排除在外——例如普通科学家就是其一。(48) 我之所以把他排除在外，是因为尽管他的研究成果可能有助于解决道德问题，但他承担的任务仅仅是研究这些问题的事实层面。像其他人一样，他在履行日常职责时也会遇到道德问题——他不应伪造实验、编造证据或篡改报告。(49) 但是，他的首要任务并不是思考支配自己行为的道德准则，正如人们并不指望商人把精力用于探究商业行为规范一样。在一生中大部分清醒的时间里，他会把自己的准则视为理所当然，就像商人把自己的道德规范视为理所当然一样。

(50) They may teach very well, and more than earn their salaries, but most of them make little or no independent reflections on human problems which involve moral judgment. This description even fits the majority of eminent scholars. Being learned in some branch of human knowledge is one thing; living in "public and illustrious thoughts," as Emerson would say, is something else.
这一定义也将大多数教师排除在外，尽管教书育人历来是许多知识分子借以谋生的手段。(50) 他们可能教得很好，而且不只是为了挣薪水而教书，但他们当中大多数人对涉及道德判断的人类问题很少或根本不进行独立的思考。这一评价甚至适用于大多数知名学者。在人类知识的某一分支上博学是一回事；正如爱默生所说，生活于“公众的、卓越的思想”之中则是另一回事。

data.title: 图画作文：偶像崇拜（贝克汉姆）
data.directions_en: 52. Directions: Study the following photos carefully and write an essay in which you should 1) describe the photos briefly, 2) interpret the social phenomenon reflected by them, and 3) give your point of view. You should write 160-200 words neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. (20 points) Note: Beckham — a British football star.
data.directions_zh: 52. 题目要求：仔细观察下面的照片，写一篇文章，内容包括：1）简要描述照片；2）解释照片反映的社会现象；3）给出你的观点。请在答题卡2上工整地写160—200词。（20分）注：贝克汉姆——英国足球明星。
data.image_desc: 两张照片：一张写有'把崇拜写在脸上'——一个年轻人脸上写着球星贝克汉姆的名字；另一张写有'花300元做小贝头'——一个小伙子正在理发店花钱请人把自己的发型做成贝克汉姆的发型。
sample: The two photos present a striking scene of star worship. In one, a young man has the name of the British football star Beckham written across his face; in the other, another youth pays 300 yuan to have his hair cut into the "Beckham style" at a barbershop. For both of them, imitating their idol seems to have become the most important thing in life.
这两张照片呈现了令人瞩目的追星场景。一张照片中，一个年轻人把英国球星贝克汉姆的名字写在脸上；另一张照片中，另一个小伙子花300元在理发店做了一个“小贝头”。对他们两人来说，模仿偶像似乎已成了生活中最重要的事。

sentences.en: For both of them, imitating their idol seems to have become the most important thing in life.
sentences.zh: 对他们两人来说，模仿偶像似乎已成了生活中最重要的事。

sample: The photos reflect a social phenomenon widespread among today's young people: blind worship of celebrities. Admiring a star for his diligence and skill is natural, but copying his name and hairstyle at any cost goes far beyond reasonable admiration. Such fanaticism wastes money and energy, and what is worse, it may lead young people to neglect their studies and lose their own individuality while chasing the shadow of an idol.
照片反映了当今年轻人中普遍存在的一种社会现象：对名人的盲目崇拜。因球星的勤奋和技艺而欣赏他本是人之常情，但不惜代价地复制他的名字和发型，则远远超出了理性欣赏的范围。这种狂热浪费金钱和精力，更糟的是，它可能使年轻人在追逐偶像影子的过程中荒废学业、丧失自我。

sample: In my view, we should take a sensible attitude toward stars. What makes Beckham great is not his haircut but his professionalism and perseverance; that is the part worth learning. Only in this way can admiration become a driving force for self-improvement instead of a blind imitation that leads us nowhere.
